lines.japanese:
「と、いうわけで、
今日から軽音楽同好会に加わることになった…」
lines.english: “And so, starting today, our newest member of the Light Music Club is…”

lines.japanese:
「…冬馬かずさ。
みんなよろしく」
lines.english: “…Kazusa Touma. Everyone, say hello.”

lines.japanese:
小木曽一人の盛大な拍手とともに、
軽音楽同好会新入部員の『他者紹介』は終わった。
lines.english: With Ogiso providing thunderous applause all by herself, Touma’s introduction—delivered entirely by someone else—came to an end.

lines.japanese:
昨夜はあんなに喋ったって言うのに、
すぐに機嫌が悪くなったり、ちょっと悪くなったり、
すごく悪くなったりと、ころころ変わる奴だ。
lines.english: For someone who had talked so much last night, she could still cycle through bad, worse, and absolutely foul moods in no time.

lines.japanese:
「で、こっちが飯塚武也。
一応ここの会長兼ギター」
lines.english: “This is Takeya Iizuka. He’s technically the club president, and our guitarist.”

lines.japanese: 「本当に連れてきやがった…」
lines.english: “You actually brought her…”

lines.japanese: 「よ、よろしく…」
lines.english: “N-Nice to meet you…”

lines.japanese: 「は、はは、は…」
lines.english: “Ha. Ha ha… ha…”
“Oh. Right…”

lines.japanese:
そういえばこいつ、
冬馬口説いて蹴りを食らったことがあるんだっけ。
lines.english: I’d forgotten: Takeya had once tried to pick Touma up and got kicked for his trouble.

lines.japanese: 「春希ぃ…」
lines.english: “Harukiii…”

lines.japanese:
「で、こっちが…
ま、よく知ってると思うけど、小木曽雪菜。
ボーカル担当で…」
lines.english: “And this is… well, you probably know her already. Setsuna Ogiso. She’s our vocalist, and…”

lines.japanese:
個人的な理由で、武也の件をフォローしないまま、
滞りなく議題を進めていく。
lines.english: For reasons of my own, I left Takeya hanging and moved briskly on.

lines.japanese:
「よろしくね冬馬さん。
あと、わたしのことは雪菜でいいよ」
lines.english: “It’s nice to meet you, Touma. And you can just call me Setsuna.”

lines.japanese: 「あたしのことはかずさで良くないから」
lines.english: “Don’t take that as permission to call me Kazusa.”
“Um…”
“Oh boy…”

lines.japanese:
この場で冬馬が初めて発した言葉は、
超友好的に接してくる小木曽に対しての、
あからさまな防波堤だった。
lines.english: The first words Touma had spoken since entering were a wall thrown up against Ogiso’s relentless friendliness.

lines.japanese:
「あ、あは…
とにかく、学園祭に向けて頑張ろ、ね？」
lines.english: “Ahaha… Anyway, let’s make this festival performance work, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「わかってる…」
lines.english: “I know…”

lines.japanese:
昨夜、小木曽から電話がかかってきたのは、
いわゆる２５時…午前１時に差し掛かった頃だった。
lines.english: Ogiso had called late the night before—just before one in the morning.

lines.japanese:
なんでも、今の今まで父親と論戦を続けていたらしく、
いつもの鈴を鳴らしたような声はなりを潜め、
妙に息遣いの色っぽいハスキーボイスとなっていた。
lines.english: Apparently she had been arguing with her father until that very moment. Her usual bell-clear voice had given way to a breathy huskiness that sounded oddly seductive.

lines.japanese: でも、声の調子そのものは、思いっきり弾んでいて…
lines.english: Despite that, she sounded utterly exhilarated.

lines.japanese:
つまりそれが、小木曽の同好会復帰と、
冬馬の同好会参加が決まった瞬間だった。
lines.english: That call marked the moment Ogiso returned to the club—and Touma agreed to join it.

lines.japanese:
よっぽど嬉しかったのか、
小木曽はその後も俺と２時間も電話でお喋りし…
lines.english: Ogiso must have been ecstatic, because she went on talking to me for another two hours.

lines.japanese:
『今から冬馬さんのところに電話するね』と、
午前３時になって言い出して、俺の説教を呼び込んだ。
lines.english: Then, at three in the morning, she announced, “I’m going to call Touma now,” earning herself a lecture from me.

lines.japanese:
「あ、ところで北原くん。
北原くんも、わたしのことは…」
lines.english: “Oh, by the way, Kitahara. You can call me…”

lines.japanese: 「小木曽どうした小木曽？」
lines.english: “What is it, Ogiso? Something wrong, Ogiso?”

lines.japanese: 『雪菜でいいよ』
lines.english: “You can call me Setsuna.”

lines.japanese:
実は、昨夜の電話の中でも、
何度か、この悪魔の囁きを聞いた記憶がある。
lines.english: Come to think of it, I remembered hearing that devil’s whisper several times during last night’s call.

lines.japanese:
けどまだ今の俺には、
この、小木曽の真名を呼んでしまった直後の自分を
制御できる自信がないから。
lines.english: But I still wasn’t confident I could control myself after speaking Ogiso’s true name aloud.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ところで雪菜ちゃ…」
lines.english: “Oh, hey, Setsu—”

lines.japanese: 「武也ぁぁぁぁぁぁっ！」
lines.english: “TAKEYAAAA!”

lines.japanese: 「うわあああああっ！？」
lines.english: “WAAAAAAH!?”

lines.japanese: ほら、制御できないし。
lines.english: See? I couldn’t control myself.

lines.japanese:
「さ、さてと…
それじゃミーティング始めます」
lines.english: “R-Right, then… Let’s get this meeting started.”

lines.japanese:
何故だか部長が戦意喪失してしまったので、
僭越ながら俺がこの場を仕切ることになった。
lines.english: With our president mysteriously robbed of the will to fight, I took the liberty of running the meeting.

lines.japanese:
なお、肝心の部長はいつもの自信と軽薄さを失い、
教室の隅で椅子に腰掛けてガタガタと震えている。
lines.english: The president himself, stripped of his usual confidence and swagger, sat trembling in a corner of the classroom.

lines.japanese: 冬馬の蹴飛ばした椅子、凄い音がしたもんなぁ。
lines.english: The chair Touma kicked had made one hell of a noise.

lines.japanese:
「ええと、それじゃどうしようかな？
とりあえずメンバーも集まったことだし…」
lines.english: “All right, where do we start? Now that we’ve got the band together, I suppose we could…”

lines.japanese: 「…集まった？」
lines.english: “…Together?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや…」
lines.english: “Ah. Well…”

lines.japanese:
「あんた、昨日のあたしの話何も聞いてなかったの？
どの面下げてそんな世迷い言を口に出せるわけ？」
lines.english: “Did you listen to anything I said yesterday? How can you stand there and spout that nonsense with a straight face?”

lines.japanese:
「い、いや、聞いてた聞いてた。
そうそう、ベースとドラムだよな」
lines.english: “I did! Of course I did. Right—the bass and drums.”

lines.japanese:
俺は狼狽しつつも、冬馬に遮られなければ言うはずだった
『一通り合わせてみようか』を口にしていないで
本当に良かった、と胸をなで下ろしていた。
lines.english: Even as I floundered, I thanked heaven she’d interrupted before I could suggest that we all try playing together.

lines.japanese:
「確かに四人いれば普通バンドは組めるけど、
それが専任ボーカルとギター二人とキーボードとなれば
全然話は別」
lines.english: “Four people might be enough for an ordinary band. But when the lineup is a singer with no instrument, two guitarists, and a keyboardist, that’s another story.”

lines.japanese: 「だ、だから…それはおいおい…」
lines.english: “Th-That’s why I thought we’d deal with that as we went…”

lines.japanese:
「大体、何の曲をやるかも決まってないのに、
メンバー揃ったとか、なんて短絡的な…」
lines.english: “You haven’t even chosen the songs. Declaring the band complete now is unbelievably shortsighted.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、わたしやりたい曲あるんだけど…」
lines.english: “Actually, there’s a song I’d like to do…”

lines.japanese: 「小木曽…？」
lines.english: “Ogiso?”

lines.japanese:
そんな俺の約束された窮地を見かねてか、
小木曽がおずおずと手を上げた。
lines.english: Perhaps taking pity on my inevitable doom, Ogiso timidly raised her hand.

lines.japanese:
「…って、今言っちゃっていいのかな？
大事な話の途中だったみたいだけど」
lines.english: “Is it okay to say it now? It sounded like you were in the middle of something important.”

lines.japanese:
「全然！　冬馬の言うとおり、
何をやるか決めないと何も進まないから。
な、そうだろ冬馬？」
lines.english: “Absolutely! Touma’s right—we can’t do anything until we pick a song. Right, Touma?”

lines.japanese:
「…うん、大丈夫、大丈夫だから。
で、なんて曲？」
lines.english: “No problem. Really, it’s fine. So what song?”

lines.japanese:
うん、大丈夫だ。
後で俺が叱られておけば…
lines.english: Yes, perfectly fine. Provided I took my scolding later…

lines.japanese: 「わかんないかなぁ？　二人とも」
lines.english: “You two can’t guess?”

lines.japanese:
「俺たちが？
小木曽の歌いたい曲を？」
lines.english: “We’re supposed to know which song you want to sing?”

lines.japanese:
「じゃあヒントね。
第３ヒントくらいまでに正解してくれなくちゃ、
lines.english: “I’ll give you hints, then. If you don’t have it by the third one,

lines.japanese: わたし泣くよ？」
lines.english: I’m going to cry, okay?”

lines.japanese:
「え？　いや、ちょっと待って！
そんな重要な曲って…」
lines.english: “What? Wait—it’s that important to you?”

lines.japanese:
「まずは第１ヒント。
わたしたちの…」
lines.english: “Here’s the first hint. What was the song that brought us—”

lines.japanese: 「『ＷＨＩＴＥ　ＡＬＢＵＭ』…」
lines.english: “White Album…”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「………出逢いの曲と言えば何でしょう？
lines.english: “…together?

lines.japanese: 冬馬さん正解」
lines.english: Correct, Touma.”

lines.japanese: 「…常識問題だし」
lines.english: “…It was obvious.”

lines.japanese: 「えへ…」
lines.english: “Hehe…”

lines.japanese: 「………早押し弱いんだよ俺」
lines.english: “…I’ve never been good at buzzer quizzes.”

lines.japanese:
その言葉が負け惜しみだってことは、
自分が一番良く知っていたけれど。
lines.english: I knew better than anyone that it was only sour grapes.

lines.japanese: いや、本気で悔しかったんだけど。
lines.english: No, I really was sore about losing.

lines.japanese:
でも、あのときのことを、
冬馬まで、こんなに鮮明に覚えているなんて、
やっぱり意表を突かれたことだけは確かだった。
lines.english: What caught me completely off guard was that Touma remembered that day so vividly too.

lines.japanese: いや、本気で嬉しかったんだけど、ね。
lines.english: Though really, I was genuinely happy too.

lines.japanese: 「俺の存在を認識してるか？　春希～」
lines.english: “Do you even remember I’m here, Haruki?”

lines.japanese: 「『ＷＨＩＴＥ　ＡＬＢＵＭ』…」
lines.english: “White Album…”

lines.japanese:
「また随分と懐かしい曲だな…
あれ何年前だ？」
lines.english: “Now that’s a blast from the past. How many years ago was it?”

lines.japanese:
「懐かしいとか言うな。
不朽の名曲だぞ」
lines.english: “Don’t call it a throwback. It’s a timeless classic.”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱりドラムとベースがネック…」
lines.english: “The drums and bass are still the main problem…”

lines.japanese:
「また、この歌の季節が来るよね。
…学園祭の頃だと、ちょっと早いけど」
lines.english: “The season for that song will be here again soon. Though the festival’s a little early.”

lines.japanese:
「ま、白い雪が街に優しく積もるのは、
早くて来月以降だろうけどな」
lines.english: “The white snow probably won’t start falling softly over the city until next month at the earliest.”

lines.japanese: 「お前だって知ってんじゃん」
lines.english: “See? You know it too.”

lines.japanese: 「間奏にサックスも入るし…」
lines.english: “And there’s a saxophone in the instrumental break…”

lines.japanese:
「当たり前だ。
懐かしいとは言ったが知らないとは言ってない。
…けど俺、どっちかと言えば緒方理奈派だな」
lines.english: “Of course I know it. I called it a throwback; I never said I hadn’t heard of it. Though personally, I’m more of a Rina Ogata guy.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ミーハーだ」
lines.english: “Look at you, chasing the hits.”

lines.japanese: 「メジャー指向だよねぇ」
lines.english: “You do go for the mainstream choice.”

lines.japanese:
「どうやって形にする？
何を捨てて、何を取る？」
lines.english: “How do we make this work?What do we cut, and what do we keep?”

lines.japanese:
「実力があるアーティストを評価してるの。それだけ。
何だよお前、緒方理奈嫌いなのかよ？」
lines.english: “I recognize talent when I see it. That’s all. What, you don’t like Rina Ogata?”

lines.japanese: 「んな訳ないじゃん」
lines.english: “Of course not.”

lines.japanese:
「この間の最新アルバムも買ったよ。
しかも初回限定版」
lines.english: “I bought her latest album too—the limited first pressing.”

lines.japanese:
「４人…ボーカルにギターにギターにキーボード。
偏ってるなぁ。
せめて誰か１人をドラムに…」
lines.english: “Four people… vocals, guitar, guitar, keyboard.What a lopsided lineup.If I could at least put one of them on drums…”

lines.japanese:
「お、いいなぁ。
俺、初回逃して未だに手に入れてないんだよな」
lines.english: “Nice. I missed the first pressing and still haven’t found a copy.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、じゃあ貸してあげる。
明日持ってくればいいかな？」
lines.english: “Then I’ll lend you mine. Want me to bring it tomorrow?”

lines.japanese:
「マジ？　悪い。
じゃさ、俺もお返しに何か…」
lines.english: “Really? Thanks. Then I should lend you something in return…”

lines.japanese:
「…何でそんなに仲いいんだお前ら？
ミス峰城大付と堅物委員長のくせに」
lines.english: “Why are you two so close? You’re Miss Houjou High and the uptight class rep.”

lines.japanese:
「その言い方やめて欲しいなぁ。
今になって、色々と人生損しちゃったって
思い知らされてるし」
lines.english: “I wish you wouldn’t call me that. I’m only now realizing how much of life I’ve missed out on.”

lines.japanese:
「やっぱ後悔してるのか？
ミス峰城大付になっちまったこと」
lines.english: “So you regret becoming Miss Houjou High?”

lines.japanese:
「うん、そうだね。
危うく堅物委員長さんと知り合わないまま
卒業しちゃうところだったから…」
lines.english: “I suppose I do. I almost made it all the way to graduation without ever getting to know our uptight class rep…”
“Huh…?”

lines.japanese:
「………なぁ春希。
俺は今、夢を見てるってことにしていいか？
それも相当にタチの良くない悪夢を」
lines.english: “…Haruki. Can I pretend this is a dream? A particularly nasty nightmare?”

lines.japanese: 「…ねぇ、ちょっと黙っててくれる？」
lines.english: “Could you be quiet for a minute?”

lines.japanese: 「聞いてたのか冬馬！？」
lines.english: “You were listening, Touma?!”

lines.japanese: 「え？　何を？」
lines.english: “What? Listening to what?”

lines.japanese:
「…冬馬に全然関係のない、
箸にも棒にもかからない雑談をだ」
lines.english: “…To our completely pointless conversation, which had absolutely nothing to do with you.”
“…Pfft.”

lines.japanese:
今の俺の状況を小木曽に笑われるのは、
甚だ遺憾だと思うんだ。
lines.english: I strongly objected to being laughed at by one of the people directly implicated in my present predicament.
lines.japaneseRuby:
今の俺の状況を[R小木曽^とうじしゃ]に笑われるのは、
甚だ遺憾だと思うんだ。

lines.japanese:
「無駄話ばかりで悪かった。
さ、議事を進めようか！」
lines.english: “Enough chitchat. Now, let’s get back to business!”
“…Mr. President.”

lines.japanese:
「なんだ冬馬？
一発逆転起死回生の凄い手でも思いつい………部長？」
lines.english: “What is it, Touma? Have you thought of some brilliant way to turn everything arou—President?”

lines.japanese:
俺たちの雑談にも加わらず、キレもせず、
ひたすら何か考え事をしていた冬馬が
最初に問いかけたのは…
lines.english: Touma had neither joined our chatter nor snapped at us, but spent the whole time lost in thought. And her first question was…

lines.japanese: 「あんた、打ち込みできる？」
lines.english: “Can you program backing tracks?”

lines.japanese:
意外な相手への、
意外な質問だった。
lines.english: An unexpected question, aimed at an even more unexpected person.

lines.japanese: 「え？　あ、ええと、それって…」
lines.english: “What? Um, you mean…”

lines.japanese: 「シンセ使えるかって意味」
lines.english: “Can you use a synthesizer?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いや、意味はわかるけど…」
lines.english: “I know what you meant, but…”

lines.japanese: 「なら質問に答えろ」
lines.english: “Then answer the question.”

lines.japanese: 「ひっ…」
lines.english: “Eek…”

lines.japanese:
「だから冬馬…
あまりドスを利かせるなと…」
lines.english: “Touma, I told you not to put so much menace in your voice…”

lines.japanese:
ただでさえ、その綺麗な顔で凄まれると、
男としては必要以上に萎縮してしまうのは
何度も経験済みだし。
lines.english: I'd learned that much firsthand. When Touma turned that beautiful face on you and growled, a man couldn't help shrinking a little more than his pride could stand.

lines.japanese:
「時間がないの。
だからさっさと答え…てくださいませんか？」
lines.english: “We’re running out of time. So answer me alrea—would you please?”

lines.japanese:
だからってその取って付けたような丁寧語は
ものすごくやっつけ感が漂うんだけど…
lines.english: But that last-second veneer of politeness could hardly have sounded more perfunctory.

lines.japanese:
「そりゃまぁ、ある程度は。
けど打ち込みなら…」
lines.english: “I know my way around it, more or less. But if you need programmed tracks…”

lines.japanese: 「冬馬、それだったら俺が…」
lines.english: “Touma, I can handle that—”

lines.japanese:
「ＯＫ部長。今後は練習に参加しなくていいから。
むしろ学校来なくていいから。
あたしの指示通り、ひたすら一人でコツコツ打ち込め」
lines.english: “Okay, Mr. President. From now on, you don’t have to come to rehearsals. In fact, don’t even come to school. Just do exactly what I tell you and spend all your time programming tracks by yourself.”
“What?”
“What?”

lines.japanese:
意外な相手への意外な質問は、
恐るべき指令となって、
軽音楽同好会の創設者を吹き飛ばした。
lines.english: That unexpected question, aimed at an even more unexpected person, turned into an order so devastating it blew the club’s own founder clean out of the band.

lines.japanese:
「必要な機材とかは後で家の方に送るから。
もう帰っていいわよ。今日はご苦労様」
lines.english: “I’ll have whatever equipment you need sent to your house later. You can go home now. That’ll be all for today.”

lines.japanese:
「って、おい！
ちょっと待て！」
lines.english: “Hey! Hold on a minute!”

lines.japanese:
しかも、ついさっき参入した、最新参メンバーによって。
…まぁ、鳴り物入りではあったけど。
lines.english: And all this from the newest member, who had joined only moments ago. Granted, she’d come in with plenty of fanfare.

lines.japanese:
「今のメンバー構成なら、
誰かがやらなくちゃならない事なの。
絶対的にパートが足りないのよ」
lines.english: “Someone has to do it with this lineup. We simply don’t have enough parts covered.”

lines.japanese:
「シンセ使うのはいいよ。
メンバー足りないんだから仕方ない。
けど、それなら俺が…」
lines.english: “I don’t mind using synth tracks. We’re short on people, so we have no choice. But if anyone’s going to program them, I should—”

lines.japanese:
「北原はまず人並みに弾けるようになれ。
話はそれからだ」
lines.english: “Kitahara, learn to play as well as an average human being first. Then we’ll talk.”

lines.japanese: 「ああっ！？」
lines.english: “What the hell!?”

lines.japanese: 「と、冬馬さん…」
lines.english: “T-Touma…”

lines.japanese:
こいつの鳴らす音は
いつもあんなに優しくフォローしてくれたのに、
こいつの喋る声はどうしてこんなに容赦がないんだろう…
lines.english: Whenever she played, her music had always supported me so gently. So why was she so merciless whenever she opened her mouth?

lines.japanese:
「とにかくまずはドラム。
少なくとも１曲目は今週中に欲しい。できる？
ま、できなくてもやってもらうんだけど」
lines.english: “First, the drums. I want the drum track for at least the first song by the end of this week. Can you do that? Well, you’re doing it either way.”

lines.japanese:
「だ、だから冬馬…
打ち込みなら俺がやるってば。
…前から俺の担当だったんだし」
lines.english: “I’m telling you, Touma, I’ll program it. That was always my job anyway.”

lines.japanese: というか、楽器演奏以外のパートは全部俺だったというか。
lines.english: Come to think of it, every job except actually playing an instrument had been mine.

lines.japanese:
皆の練習時間が合わないことも多くて、
練習用に全パート分作ったから、ギターの練習以上に
時間を取られてたような気もするけど。
lines.english: Our schedules rarely lined up, so I’d programmed every part for rehearsals. Come to think of it, that may have taken more time than practicing guitar.

lines.japanese:
「だからさ、武也をギターに残して、
俺が打ち込みに回った方がいいんじゃないか？」
lines.english: “So wouldn’t it make more sense to keep Takeya on guitar and put me on the backing tracks?”

lines.japanese: 「あたしは別にそれでも異存はないけど…」
lines.english: “I’d be fine with that too…”

lines.japanese:
「な？　その方が絶対に適材適所だって。
なるべく成功率を上げた方が…」
lines.english: “Right? It’s obviously the best use of both of us. We ought to give ourselves the best chance of succeeding—”

lines.japanese:
「ただ、今の事実を、
北原が小木曽にちゃんと説明できるなら、だけど」
lines.english: “Provided you can explain one little fact to Ogiso first.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
「？　どういうこと？
北原くんと飯塚くんの受け持ちが代わると、
何がどうなるの？」
lines.english: “What do you mean? What changes if Kitahara and Iizuka swap jobs?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、それは…」
lines.english: “Well, that’s…”

lines.japanese:
「さあ、話してみたら？
学園祭当日、あんたが小木曽の隣にいないってこと…」
lines.english: “Go on, tell her. Tell her you won’t be standing beside her on the day of the festival.”

lines.japanese: 「は…春希？」
lines.english: “H-Haruki?”

lines.japanese: 「北原くん？」
lines.english: “Kitahara?”

lines.japanese: …詰んだ。
lines.english: …Checkmate.

lines.japanese: 「うおおおおおぉぉぉぉぉぉ～！」
lines.english: “NOOOOOOOOO!”

lines.japanese:
さらば飯塚武也。
君のことは忘れない。
lines.english: Farewell, Takeya Iizuka. I’ll never forget you.

lines.japanese:
「さて、学園祭当日まであと二週間。
二人とも、泣いても笑ってもいいけど、
投げ出したら殴るから」
lines.english: “The festival is two weeks away. Laugh, cry—I don’t care. But if either of you gives up, I’ll hit you.”

lines.japanese: 「お、おう…」
lines.english: “R-Right…”

lines.japanese:
「…凄いね。
北原くんが冬馬さんのことあれだけ欲しがったの、
こうしてみるとよくわかる…」
lines.english: “She’s incredible. Now that I’ve seen her like this, I understand why you wanted her so badly…”

lines.japanese: 「お…おう…」
lines.english: “R-Right…”

lines.japanese: いきなり仕切ることまでは予想してなかったけどな…
lines.english: I hadn’t expected her to take charge on the spot, though…

lines.japanese:
「残りの曲はおいおい考えていくとして、
まずは１曲目だけでも今週中に仕上げておかないと」
lines.english: “We can choose the rest of the songs as we go. But we need at least one finished by the end of this week.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだな…」
lines.english: “Right…”

lines.japanese:
俺が『おいおい考えていく』使ったら、
あんなに怒ったくせに…
lines.english: She’d nearly bitten my head off when I said we could figure things out as we went.

lines.japanese:
「それじゃ、時間がないからとりあえず合わせるか。
…小木曽」
lines.english: “We’re short on time, so let’s just run through it once. …Ogiso.”

lines.japanese:
「うんっ。
あと、わたしのことは雪菜でいいよ」
lines.english: “Okay! And you can call me Setsuna.”

lines.japanese:
俺が『とりあえず合わせる』なんて言ったら、
絶対に呆れた目で睨むくせに…
lines.english: If I’d said, “Let’s just run through it once,” she would have given me a look of utter disgust…

lines.japanese:
「キーは原曲のまんまで行けるんだよね？
発声練習する？」
lines.english: “You can sing it in the original key, right? Do you need to warm up?”

lines.japanese:
「ごめん、合唱部とか入ったことないから
やり方わかんないんだ。
いつも歌いながら声出してくから」
lines.english: “Sorry, I’ve never been in a choir, so I don’t really know how. I usually warm up by singing.”

lines.japanese:
「ま、仕方ないか。
じゃ、ぶっつけで行くから…いい？　小木曽」
lines.english: “Nothing we can do about that. We’ll go in cold, then. Ready, Ogiso?”

lines.japanese: 「…はぁい」
lines.english: “…Okaaay.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、ちょっと待ってくれ。
まだ俺の準備が…」
lines.english: “Wait a second. I’m not ready yet…”

lines.japanese:
いつの間にか準備万端な二人に置いてかれないよう、
俺も慌ててケースからギターを取り出し…
lines.english: Before I knew it, both of them were ready. I hurried to pull my guitar from its case before they left me behind—

lines.japanese:
「…何言ってるんだ北原？
なぜあたしたちがお前を待つ必要がある？」
lines.english: “What are you talking about, Kitahara? Why should we wait for you?”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
たところで、冬馬から浴びせられた言葉は、
なかなかに慈悲浅き響きを含んでいた。
lines.english: —and was met with a reply conspicuously short on mercy.

lines.japanese: 「だって、合わせるんじゃ？」
lines.english: “Aren’t we playing together?”

lines.japanese: 「小木曽のボーカルと、あたしのピアノをね」
lines.english: “I meant Ogiso on vocals and me on piano.”

lines.japanese: 「…俺のギターは？」
lines.english: “…What about my guitar?”

lines.japanese: 「今のレベルなら邪魔」
lines.english: “At your level, you’d only get in the way.”

lines.japanese: 「うっ…」
lines.english: “Urgh…”

lines.japanese: 「と、冬馬さん…」
lines.english: “T-Touma…”

lines.japanese:
「今日のところは小木曽の力を見たい。
他の面倒見てる暇ないから」
lines.english: “Today, I want to hear what Ogiso can do. I don’t have time to babysit anyone else.”

lines.japanese:
他…
面倒…
暇…
lines.english: Anyone else… Babysit… No time…

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、じゃあ、俺は？」
lines.english: “Then what am I supposed to do?”

lines.japanese:
あの、二つの音楽室と屋上で重ねたセッションは…
俺たちの、初めての出逢いの日は…
lines.english: What about all the times we'd played together, in the two music rooms and up on the roof? What about the day we'd first met?

lines.japanese:
「第一で自主練してきたら？
隣も借りてるんでしょ？」
lines.english: “Practice by yourself in Music Room One. We reserved that room too, didn’t we?”

lines.japanese: 「き、北原くん…」
lines.english: “K-Kitahara…”

lines.japanese: 「なに？　文句があるって？」
lines.english: “What? Do you have a complaint?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、その…」
lines.english: “No, I…”

lines.japanese:
加入一日目で部長を排除し、
さらに残る古参メンバーまでも練習から除外し。
lines.english: On her very first day, she had expelled the president and barred the club’s only other veteran member from rehearsal.

lines.japanese:
あんなに参加を嫌がったのは、
この恐るべき専制君主ぶりを隠すためだったのか…
lines.english: Was that why she had fought so hard not to join—so no one would discover what a terrifying tyrant she was?

lines.japanese:
「不満があるならさ、文句を言わせない実力と、
現実的なビジョンを示せば良かったのに。
そしたら喜んで従ったよ？　『部長代理』」
lines.english: “If you don’t like it, you should’ve shown me enough skill to leave no room for complaint, and a plan that could actually work. I’d have been happy to follow you then, ‘Mr. Acting President.’”

lines.japanese: 「あ、北原くんっ！」
lines.english: “Kitahara!”

lines.japanese: 「始めるよ、小木曽」
lines.english: “We’re starting, Ogiso.”

lines.japanese: 「で、でも…」
lines.english: “B-But…”

lines.japanese: 「…始める。いいね？」
lines.english: “We’re starting. Understood?”
“…Okaaay.”

lines.japanese: 「うおおおおおぉぉぉぉぉぉ～！」
lines.english: “NOOOOOOOOO!”

lines.japanese:
「はぁ、はぁ、はぁ…
う、うう…ううう…」
lines.english: “Hah… hah… Ugh… ngh…”

lines.japanese:
さらば北原春希。
俺のことは忘れない…
lines.english: Farewell, Haruki Kitahara. Don’t forget me…

lines.japanese: 「…練習しよっと」
lines.english: “…Guess I’ll practice.”

lines.japanese: 午後八時。
lines.english: Eight p.m.

lines.japanese:
見回りの警備員にいい加減怒られ、
校舎を追い出された時には、
晩秋の夜はとっくに更けまくっていた。
lines.english: By the time the security guard finally lost patience and threw us out, night had long since fallen over the late-autumn streets.

lines.japanese: 「…あのさ」
lines.english: “Hey…”
“…What?”

lines.japanese:
徒歩通学の小木曽と駅前で別れ、
同じ上り電車で帰路につく冬馬と俺は、
およそ一駅間失っていた会話を、やっと復活させた。
lines.english: After parting with Ogiso outside the station—she lived close enough to walk to school—Touma and I caught the same train home. It took us nearly a full stop to revive the conversation we'd let die.

lines.japanese:
「どうかな、小木曽の歌？
俺的には相当いい線行ってると思うんだけど」
lines.english: “What did you think of Ogiso’s singing? I thought she was pretty damn good.”

lines.japanese:
「…そうね。
確かに素人だけど、上手い部類に入る。
というか、普通の人間はあの声だけで騙される」
lines.english: “She was. Obviously untrained, but still good. Most people would hear that voice and never notice.”

lines.japanese:
というか、三人でいるときも、
ほとんど小木曽が会話を振っていたから、
実際には、数時間ぶりの会話になるのかも。
lines.english: Then again, with the three of us together, Ogiso had been the one to keep almost every conversation going. Maybe this was the first time Touma and I had really spoken in hours.

lines.japanese:
「だよな！　俺の見込んだ通りだ。
さすがヒトカラの女王！」
lines.english: “I knew it! Just as I predicted. All hail the queen of solo karaoke!”

lines.japanese: 「…それって領民は一人もいないんじゃ？」
lines.english: “…A queen without a single subject?”

lines.japanese:
小木曽としては、
冬馬に排除された俺と、
俺を弾いた冬馬に気を使ったんだろうけど。
lines.english: Ogiso had probably been trying to be considerate of both sides: me, whom Touma had shut out, and Touma, who’d done the shutting out.

lines.japanese:
「ま、まぁ、それはともかく。
これでボーカルの方は目処がついたかな？」
lines.english: “Well, never mind that. So we’re set for vocals?”

lines.japanese:
「そっちは最初からアテにしてた。
むしろ問題なのはそれ以外」
lines.english: “I was counting on her from the beginning. Everything else is the problem.”

lines.japanese:
でも、そんな些細なことを気にする俺じゃない。
俺たちが学園祭のステージで輝くためには、
避けては通れない道だから。
lines.english: But I wasn’t about to let a little thing like that get to me. If we wanted our moment onstage at the festival, there was no getting around it.

lines.japanese:
「まずはベース？
まぁ、俺も明日からもう一度当たってみるけど」
lines.english: “The bass comes first, then? I’ll start asking around again tomorrow.”

lines.japanese:
「へぇ？
たった一日で、
人の心配ができるレベルにまで上達したんだ？」
lines.english: “Oh? After one day, you’ve already improved enough to worry about other people?”
“Ah…”

lines.japanese: …いや、だから全然気にしてないんだって。
lines.english: No, really. It didn’t bother me at all.

lines.japanese:
「え…ええと、北原。
それでその、だな…」
lines.english: “Um… Kitahara. About that…”
“…What?”

lines.japanese:
そこまで一瞬で後悔するくらいなら
嫌味を言わなければいいのにと思わなくもないけど。
lines.english: If she was going to regret it that quickly, you’d think she would learn not to make those jabs in the first place.

lines.japanese:
まぁ、そこが冬馬の冬馬たる所以というか、
俺が全然気に入ってなくないアンバランスな性格というか。
lines.english: But that was what made Touma who she was—one of those off-kilter things about her that I didn’t exactly dislike.

lines.japanese: 「お前、家で練習できる？」
lines.english: “Can you practice at home?”

lines.japanese:
「マンションだから、学校みたいな風にはいかないけど、
まぁ、ヘッドフォンでなら」
lines.english: “I live in an apartment, so I can’t play the way I do at school. But I can use headphones.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか…」
lines.english: “I see…”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱ、家でも自主練しないと駄目か？」
lines.english: “Do I really need to practice at home too?”

lines.japanese:
「当たり前だ。
お前の場合、今から毎日２４時間練習しても、
間に合うかどうかってレベルなのに…」
lines.english: “Obviously. At your level, you could practice twenty-four hours a day from now on and still not be ready in time…”

lines.japanese:
で、この後悔が学習に繋がらないところも、
俺は別に気にするけど嫌いじゃない。
気にするけど。
lines.english: It did bother me that regret never taught her anything. But I didn’t hate it. It bothered me, though.

lines.japanese:
「少なくとも、
今日練習したところのおさらいを一通りやること。
ノーミスで通して弾けたら寝ていいから」
lines.english: “At the very least, review everything we covered today. You can sleep once you can play it straight through without a mistake.”

lines.japanese:
「わかった、わかったよ。
晩飯食って、勉強した後…」
lines.english: “Fine, fine. After dinner, once I’ve studied—”
“Studying!?”

lines.japanese:
「え？　いや、だって…
学園祭が終わったらすぐに期末…」
lines.english: “What? But finals start right after the festival…”

lines.japanese: 「学生の本分は…」
lines.english: “A student’s first duty is—”

lines.japanese:
「わかった、わかったよ！
ちっくしょ～、いつも準備してない奴は気楽でいいなぁ」
lines.english: “Fine, fine! Damn it. Must be nice never having to study for anything.”

lines.japanese:
昨日までとは、
完全に温度差が逆転してるような気がする。
lines.english: Compared with yesterday, our levels of enthusiasm had completely reversed.

lines.japanese:
何と言うか、
冬馬の音楽に対するこだわりは半端じゃないと言うか、
お前にはそれしかないのかと言うか…
lines.english: How could I put it? Touma’s obsession with music was something else. It was almost enough to make you wonder if she had anything else in her life…

lines.japanese:
「大体、北原だったら
とっくに峰城大への推薦取ってるでしょ？
なんで今さら勉強なんかする訳？」
lines.english: “Your place at Houjou University is already guaranteed, isn’t it? Why bother studying now?”
lines.japaneseRuby:
「大体、北原だったら
とっくに[R峰城大^うえ]への推薦取ってるでしょ？
なんで今さら勉強なんかする訳？」

lines.japanese:
「テストの時って一月前から勉強するものだろ？
定期だろうが実力だろうが模試だろうが」
lines.english: “You’re supposed to start studying a month before a test, whatever kind it is—term exams, proficiency tests, mock exams.”

lines.japanese:
まぁ、などという誓いを立てると、
俺みたいに一年中勉強する羽目に陥るわけだけど。
lines.english: Of course, following that rule meant ending up like me and studying all year round.

lines.japanese:
「わかってる。俺が悪かったよ。
そこまで軽蔑した目で見なくてもいいだろ」
lines.english: “I know. I was wrong. You don’t have to look at me with such contempt.”

lines.japanese: 「軽蔑なんか…してないけどさ」
lines.english: “I don’t… look down on you.”

lines.japanese:
「ああ約束する。
もう学園祭まではギターのことしか考えない。
その代わり、信じさせてもらうからな」
lines.english: “All right, I promise. Until the festival, guitar is the only thing I’ll think about. Which means I’m trusting you.”

lines.japanese: 「何を？」
lines.english: “Trusting me with what?”

lines.japanese: 「冬馬が、後は絶対に何とかしてくれるって」
lines.english: “Everything else. I’m trusting you to find a way to make it work, no matter what.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
「俺は、
自分のパートだけに全力を尽くせばいいんだって」
lines.english: “So all I have to do is give everything I’ve got to my own part.”

lines.japanese: 我ながら情けない宣言だとは思うけど…
lines.english: I knew how pathetic that sounded.

lines.japanese:
今日入ったばかりの冬馬におんぶにだっこは
みっともないけれど…
lines.english: It was humiliating to lean so completely on someone who had only joined that day.

lines.japanese: 「本当に、頼むな」
lines.english: “I’m really counting on you.”

lines.japanese: 「………任せておけば？」
lines.english: “…Then just leave it to me.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ…」
lines.english: “I will…”

lines.japanese:
でもやっぱり、
その他人事な態度が、とてつもなく頼もしい。
lines.english: And yet, the way she said it as though none of this had anything to do with her was enormously reassuring.

lines.japanese:
あの夏休みの日、初めて冬馬の奏でる音を聴いた時…
俺は、こいつに頼ることを覚えた。
lines.english: That day over summer break, the first time I heard Touma play, I learned to depend on her.

lines.japanese:
今日やっと、あの時の主従関係を取り戻した。
だからもう、心配することはやめよう。
lines.english: Today, at last, we had restored that old master-and-servant relationship. So I could stop worrying.

lines.japanese:
…端から聞いてると、
とてつもなく情けない宣言のように聞こえるのは、
多分、気のせいでも何でもないんだろうけど。
lines.english: Granted, to anyone listening, every word of this would have sounded every bit as pathetic as it was. And that was not just my imagination.

lines.japanese:
「岩津町、岩津町です。
お降りの方はドアにお気をつけください」
lines.english: “Now arriving at Iwazucho. Iwazucho. Please mind the doors as you exit.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ…」
lines.english: “Well…”

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
学園から三つ目の駅。
冬馬の家の、最寄り駅。
lines.english: The third stop from school. Touma’s stop.

lines.japanese:
何の未練もない足取りでさっさとホームに下りた冬馬は、
けれど振り向くと、もう一度正面から俺を見つめる。
lines.english: Touma stepped briskly onto the platform without a moment’s hesitation. Then she turned and looked me straight in the eye one last time.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ…」
lines.english: “Hey…”

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese:
「本当は北原も、
早めに合わせておく方がいいんだけど、な」
lines.english: “Really, we ought to start rehearsing with you before too long.”

lines.japanese: で、やっぱり口にするのはそういうことで。
lines.english: And of course, that was what she chose to worry about.

lines.japanese:
こういう心配の仕方が、
本当にこいつを仲間に引き入れておいて
良かったって実感する一瞬だったり。
lines.english: It was moments like this, when she worried in the only way she knew how, that made me glad I'd brought her into the band.

lines.japanese:
「けど、まずは小木曽が最優先だろ？
ボーカルさえきっちりしてれば、
ギターがどうなってようとあんま気にされないしな」
lines.english: “But Ogiso comes first, right? If the vocals are solid, no one pays much attention to what the guitar’s doing.”

lines.japanese: 「…ま、ぶっちゃけそうなんだけど」
lines.english: “…Honestly, yeah.”

lines.japanese:
「ドアが閉まります。
ご注意ください」
lines.english: “The doors are closing. Please stand clear.”

lines.japanese:
「だから今日のことは本当に気にしてないって。
ま、なるべく早めに俺の方も見てくれると助かるけど」
lines.english: “So I really don’t mind what happened today. Though I’d appreciate it if you could start working with me sooner rather than later.”

lines.japanese: 「…努力、するよ」
lines.english: “…I’ll try.”

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ、また明日」
lines.english: “See you tomorrow.”
“Mm…”

lines.japanese: 「うあっ…」
lines.english: “Argh…”

lines.japanese:
「くっそ～…
せっかくもう少しでノーミスだったのに」
lines.english: “Damn it! I almost made it through without a mistake.”

lines.japanese: 「…今度こそ」
lines.english: “…This time for sure.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、５分休憩」
lines.english: “All right, five-minute break.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、お疲れさま～」
lines.english: “Okay. Good work, everyone!”

lines.japanese:
「お疲れなのはそっちだから。
喉、大丈夫？」
lines.english: “You're the one who's tired. Is your throat okay?”

lines.japanese:
「ああ、心配しないで。
三時間歌いっぱなし程度ならいつもやってるから」
lines.english: “Don’t worry. I sing for three hours straight all the time.”

lines.japanese: 「………少しは休憩入れろ」
lines.english: “…Try taking a break once in a while.”

lines.japanese: 「ね、はちみつレモン作ってきたんだけど飲む？」
lines.english: “I brought some honey-lemon. Want some?”

lines.japanese: 「あたしは喉使ってないから」
lines.english: “I’m not the one who’s been singing.”

lines.japanese: 「ちゃんと三人分あるんだけどな」
lines.english: “I made enough for all three of us.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅ～、気持ちいい風」
lines.english: “Ahh, what a lovely breeze.”

lines.japanese: 「…寒い」
lines.english: “…It’s freezing.”

lines.japanese:
「…あ、北原くんのギターだ。
頑張れっ」
lines.english: “Oh, that’s Kitahara on guitar. Keep at it!”

lines.japanese: 「ヘタクソ」
lines.english: “He sucks.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ」
lines.english: “Hehe.”

lines.japanese: 「だから寒い」
lines.english: “I said it’s cold.”

lines.japanese:
「もうちょっとだけ。
休憩時間の間くらい、いいでしょ？」
lines.english: “Just a little longer. We can stay out here until the break is over, can’t we?”

lines.japanese: 「…勝手にすれば？」
lines.english: “…Suit yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、勝手にさせていただきます」
lines.english: “Thank you. I believe I will.”

lines.japanese: 「ね、冬馬さん」
lines.english: “Touma?”

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「そろそろ北原くんもこっちに呼べばいいんじゃない？」
lines.english: “Don’t you think it’s about time we invited Kitahara back in here?”

lines.japanese:
「全然。
まだまだ」
lines.english: “Not even close. He has a long way to go.”

lines.japanese:
「でもさぁ、
だいぶミスもなくなってきたみたいに聞こえるけど？」
lines.english: “Really? It sounds as if he’s hardly making any mistakes now.”

lines.japanese:
「ミスはしなくなったけど、テンポが合ってない。
難しいところになると急に遅くなってたりするし」
lines.english: “He’s stopped making mistakes, but his tempo’s wrong. He suddenly slows down whenever he reaches a difficult section.”

lines.japanese:
「だけど、もう時間ないんだよね？
そろそろみんなで合わせないと、
本番に間に合わないんじゃ？」
lines.english: “But we're running out of time, aren't we? If we don't start playing together soon, won't we be too late for the show?”

lines.japanese:
「ちゃんとあたしの計画通りに進んでる。
みんなで合わせるのは週末くらい」
lines.english: “Everything’s going according to my plan. We’ll start full-band rehearsals around the weekend.”

lines.japanese: 「もう大丈夫だと思うんだけどなぁ…」
lines.english: “I think he’s ready now…”

lines.japanese:
「小木曽は北原を過大評価し過ぎてる。
あいつはそんなにデキる奴じゃ…」
lines.english: “You’re overestimating Kitahara way too much. He’s not that capable—”

lines.japanese:
「過大評価って、
し過ぎるものでしょ？」
lines.english: “Isn’t any overestimate already too much?”

lines.japanese: 「あと、わたしのことは雪菜でいいよ」
lines.english: “And you can call me Setsuna.”

lines.japanese:
「…小木曽もあんまり北原に毒されない方がいい。
妙な揚げ足ばかり取るような腐った性格になる」
lines.english: “…You shouldn’t let Kitahara rub off on you. You’ll end up just as rotten as he is, picking apart every little thing people say.”

lines.japanese:
「…ねぇ冬馬さん？
あなたも実は結構我慢してるんじゃない？」
lines.english: “Touma… You’ve been holding yourself back too, haven’t you?”

lines.japanese:
「そんなことない。
大体なんであたしが…」
lines.english: “Of course not. Why would I—”

lines.japanese:
「合ってるよ？
北原くんのギターと」
lines.english: “You’re already playing along with Kitahara’s guitar.”

lines.japanese: 「よし、今度こそ…」
lines.english: “All right. This time…”

lines.japanese: 「うわああっ！？」
lines.english: “Waaah!?”

lines.japanese:
今日も、午後八時。
練習が始まって、もう三日。
lines.english: Eight p.m. again. Our third day of rehearsals.

lines.japanese:
見回りの警備員に、『また冬馬さんの娘さんか』と
顔をしかめられるくらいには、
冬馬家の威光を最大限に利用した三日間。
lines.english: For three straight days, we had exploited the Touma family’s pull to the hilt—enough that the guard making his rounds now frowned and said, “Youko Touma’s daughter again?”

lines.japanese: 「はぁ…」
lines.english: “Hah…”

lines.japanese: 「疲れてる？」
lines.english: “Tired?”

lines.japanese: 「全然」
lines.english: “Not at all.”

lines.japanese: 「俺はちょっと…」
lines.english: “I am, a little…”

lines.japanese:
「そういうことは先に言え。
…あたしもちょっとだけ」
lines.english: “You should’ve said so. …I’m a little tired too.”

lines.japanese: 「なんでそんなことでまで意地を張る？」
lines.english: “Why do you have to be stubborn even about that?”

lines.japanese:
いつものように、真っ暗な道を三人で歩き、
駅で一人減って電車に乗り込んだ俺たちは、
いつもよりちょっと元気のない会話を交わした。
lines.english: As always, the three of us walked the pitch-dark road to the station. There, three became two; we boarded the train and mustered a conversation a little less lively than usual.

lines.japanese: 「ふああ…」
lines.english: “Yaaawn…”

lines.japanese: 「ちゃんと寝てる？」
lines.english: “Getting enough sleep?”

lines.japanese:
「いつものことだから。
…四時間くらい」
lines.english: “The usual. About four hours.”

lines.japanese:
勉強と色々な頼まれごとをほっぽり出して、
その分の空き時間を全てギターの練習に費やしてる。
lines.english: I had let my studies and every favor people had asked of me slide, then poured all the time that freed into guitar practice.

lines.japanese:
昨夜、俺が床の上で目覚めたとき、
ギターがベッドの上で毛布にくるまれてたっけ。
lines.english: When I woke on the floor last night, the guitar was tucked into my bed under the blanket.

lines.japanese: 「なんだ、ちゃんと寝てるな」
lines.english: “Oh. So you are sleeping.”

lines.japanese: 「って、どんだけ起きてんだよ冬馬…」
lines.english: “How much sleep do you get, Touma…?”
“…Hey?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　ああ、なに？」
lines.english: “Hm? Oh. What?”

lines.japanese:
３秒で気を失いかけるって、
本当にどんだけ起きてんだ？
lines.english: She had nearly passed out in three seconds. How long had she been awake?

lines.japanese:
「俺は練習があるからわかるけど、
お前、帰ったら何してんだ？」
lines.english: “I’m exhausted because I have to practice, but what are you doing after you get home?”

lines.japanese: 「だって、学園祭が終わったらすぐに期末…」
lines.english: “Well, finals start right after the festival…”

lines.japanese: 「冗談だよな？」
lines.english: “You’re joking, right?”

lines.japanese: 「わかりやすいだろ？」
lines.english: “That was pretty obvious, wasn’t it?”

lines.japanese:
そういう冗談を俺に言ってくれること自体は
結構嬉しいんだけど、時と場合をわきまえて欲しい。
lines.english: I was honestly glad she'd joke with me at all. I just wished she'd picked a better time.

lines.japanese: 「…なんか無理してる？」
lines.english: “…Are you pushing yourself too hard?”

lines.japanese:
「別にいい。
説明したところで北原がなんとかできるわけでもないし」
lines.english: “Never mind. It’s not as if telling you would let you do anything about it.”

lines.japanese:
「もしかして、
俺って知らないところでそんなに冬馬に負担かけてる？」
lines.english: “Have I really been putting that much strain on you without even realizing it?”

lines.japanese:
「良心の呵責に押し潰される時間があるなら練習しろ。
ちゃんと１日１０時間弾いてるか？」
lines.english: “If you’ve got time to wallow in guilt, practice. You are playing ten hours a day, right?”

lines.japanese:
否定してくれない…
俺ってそんなに冬馬に負担かけてるんだ…
lines.english: She didn’t deny it… So I really was that much of a burden to her.

lines.japanese:
「前にも言ってたけど、
やっぱ毎日１０時間って必要なのか？」
lines.english: “You’ve said that before, but do I really have to practice ten hours every day?”

lines.japanese:
「３歳の頃から、クリスマスも、正月も、誕生日も、
友達と遊ぶ約束をしてても…」
lines.english: “Since I was three. Christmas, New Year’s, birthdays—even when I’d made plans with friends…”

lines.japanese:
「それに普通、
コンクールの三月前くらいから準備始めるし。
そうなったら１日１６時間くらい」
lines.english: “And normally you start preparing for a competition about three months ahead. Then it’s closer to sixteen hours a day.”

lines.japanese: 「しゅ、修学旅行は？」
lines.english: “W-What about the school trip?”

lines.japanese:
「ほんと細かい揚げ足取りばかりだな北原は。
…３年に一度くらいはそういう日もある」
lines.english: “You really do pick at every little technicality, Kitahara. Fine—once every three years or so, I might miss a day.”

lines.japanese: 「よかったぁぁぁぁ！」
lines.english: “Thank God!”

lines.japanese:
千日に１日くらいはそういう日がないと、
いくらなんでも辛すぎるだろうしな。
lines.english: One day in a thousand had to be allowed. Anything else would be too cruel.

lines.japanese:
…千日のうち９９９日くらいがああいう日ってのは、
どうなんだろうというのは考えたくもないけど。
lines.english: Though I preferred not to think about what it meant that she spent the other nine hundred and ninety-nine days like that.

lines.japanese:
「ほんと、今は天国。
一日中弾かなくてもいい日がこんなにあるなんて」
lines.english: “This is heaven. I get so many days now when I don’t have to play from morning to night.”

lines.japanese: 「…やっぱ、やめたのか？」
lines.english: “…You really did quit?”

lines.japanese: 「見切られた」
lines.english: “I got written off.”
“What?”
“Touma…?”

lines.japanese:
「で、ちゃんと弾けるようになった？
最後までミスもなく、リズムも完璧で、
相手に合わせる余裕を持てるようになったのか？」
lines.english: “So can you play it now? All the way through without mistakes, perfectly in time, with enough attention left over to follow someone else?”

lines.japanese:
それは、明らかに今までの会話を後悔した上での、
あからさまな話題のすり替えだったけれど。
lines.english: It was an absurdly obvious change of subject, born of instant regret over everything she had just admitted.

lines.japanese:
「自分ではだいぶイけてるんじゃないかと思ってるけど、
合わせられるかどうかは、合わせてみないと何とも」
lines.english: “I think I’m doing pretty well. But I won’t know whether I can play with anyone until we try.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、か」
lines.english: “R-Right.”

lines.japanese:
その転調に合わせられるくらいには、
俺の人生、練習は重ねてきたつもりだ。
lines.english: I’d had enough practice in life to follow a key change that obvious.

lines.japanese: 「もう、合わせても大丈夫、か」
lines.english: “Maybe we can try playing together now.”

lines.japanese:
「聞き違えるなよ。
合わせてみないと何とも、だ」
lines.english: “Don’t put words in my mouth. I said we won’t know until we try.”

lines.japanese: 「なら…合わせるか」
lines.english: “Then… let’s try.”

lines.japanese:
「そりゃ、願ってもないな。
じゃ、明日の放課後は…」
lines.english: “I’d love that. So tomorrow after school—”

lines.japanese:
「明日は小木曽の仕上げ。
北原に構ってる暇なんか相変わらず全然」
lines.english: “Tomorrow I’m putting the finishing touches on Ogiso’s vocals. I still won’t have any time for you, Kitahara.”

lines.japanese:
「…てことは結局、
週末までおあずけってことかよ？」
lines.english: “…So I still have to wait until the weekend?”

lines.japanese:
惜しい。
せっかく冬馬に認められそうだったのに。
lines.english: So close. Touma had almost admitted I was getting somewhere.

lines.japanese: ま、例えそれがこいつの逃げだったとしても…
lines.english: Even if she had only said it as a way out…

lines.japanese:
結局、ちょっとだけ前進しそうだった俺のステージは、
最終的には『時間切れ』という無難な結論になった。
lines.english: In the end, just when it looked as though I might finally get somewhere, we arrived at the safest possible conclusion: we had run out of time.

lines.japanese:
「岩津町、岩津町です。
お降りの方はドアにお気をつけください」
lines.english: “Now arriving at Iwazucho. Iwazucho. Please mind the doors as you exit.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ…」
lines.english: “Well…”

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
いつもの駅。
そしていつもの足取り。
lines.english: The same station. The same brisk stride.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ…」
lines.english: “Hey…”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese:
そして、いつも通りの、
電車とホームに分かたれてからの会話。
lines.english: And, as always, a conversation carried on across the divide between train and platform.

lines.japanese: 「冬馬？」
lines.english: “Touma?”

lines.japanese: …が、今日は、何だか。
lines.english: Except that tonight, for some reason…
“Hey…?”

lines.japanese:
「ドアが閉まります。
ご注意ください」
lines.english: “The doors are closing. Please stand clear.”
“What? Ah—!?”

lines.japanese: 「…おい」
lines.english: “…Hey.”

lines.japanese: 今日は、何だか…
lines.english: Tonight, for some reason…

lines.japanese: 俺の降りる駅が、違う。
lines.english: I was getting off at a different station.

lines.japanese:
電車のドアが閉じられる瞬間、
冬馬の手が、俺のネクタイに伸びて。
lines.english: Just as the train doors were closing, Touma’s hand shot out and caught my tie.

lines.japanese: そして、引きずり降ろされた。
lines.english: Then she dragged me onto the platform.

lines.japanese: 「どういうつもりだよ…冬馬？」
lines.english: “What do you think you’re doing, Touma?”

lines.japanese:
だってここは、学園から三つ目の駅。
冬馬の家の、最寄り駅。
lines.english: This was the third stop from school. Touma’s station.

lines.japanese: それって、つまり…
lines.english: Which meant…

lines.japanese: 「今から…あたしの家に来い」
lines.english: “You’re coming… home with me.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese:
そういう、あり得ない仮定しか、
想像できなかったけど…
lines.english: It was the only explanation I could imagine, impossible as it was.

lines.japanese: どうやら、あり得なくなかったらしい。
lines.english: Apparently, it wasn’t so impossible after all.

lines.japanese: 「と、冬馬…ちょと、おい」
lines.english: “T-Touma… wait a second.”

lines.japanese: 「早く…来なよ」
lines.english: “Hurry up… Come on.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、こんな…こんなことって」
lines.english: “No. This… This can’t really be happening.”

lines.japanese:
「どうしたの？
今になって怖気づいた？」
lines.english: “What’s wrong? Losing your nerve now?”

lines.japanese: 「怖気づくわそりゃあああ！」
lines.english: “OF COURSE I AM!”

lines.japanese: 現在、午後九時。
lines.english: Nine p.m.

lines.japanese: 場所はあろうことか、冬馬家の敷居の内側。
lines.english: And, against all reason, I was inside the Touma residence.

lines.japanese:
けど、それはさほど問題ではなくて。
…いや、普通ならとんでもない問題なんだけど。
lines.english: But that wasn’t the real problem. Though under ordinary circumstances it would have been an enormous one.

lines.japanese: 「ありえねえだろこれ！」
lines.english: “This is insane!”

lines.japanese:
「そう言われると思った。
だから本当は誰も呼びたくなかったんだけどな」
lines.english: “I knew you’d say that. It’s why I never wanted to invite anyone.”

lines.japanese:
冬馬家は、まず門をくぐる段階で、
岡山のボンボンの末裔をビビらせたにも関わらず、
そんな外観の豪華さは単なる序章に過ぎなかった。
lines.english: The gates alone were intimidating enough even for the heir to a wealthy Okayama family. Yet all that exterior splendor was only the prologue.

lines.japanese:
玄関を入ると、冗談みたいにデカいリビングや、
窓の外に見える手入れされた広い庭にビビる暇もなく、
いきなり階段を『下り』させられた。
lines.english: No sooner was I inside than Touma marched me down a flight of stairs, before I had time to take in the absurdly vast living room or the broad, manicured garden beyond its windows.

lines.japanese:
冬馬がその地下室の電源をつけると、
二十畳くらいの広めの白い部屋があり、
そこにはピアノを始め、沢山の楽器が転がっていた。
lines.english: Touma switched on the basement lights, revealing a broad white room about the size of a studio apartment. A piano stood among instruments strewn everywhere.

lines.japanese:
けれど何よりも俺の目を点にしたのは、
部屋の天井からぶら下がっている高そうなマイクと、
部屋の奥にある、ガラスで仕切られた狭い部屋。
lines.english: But what truly stopped me dead were the expensive-looking microphones hanging from the ceiling and the small glass-walled room at the far end.

lines.japanese: 「こ…ここは？」
lines.english: “Wh-What is this place?”

lines.japanese: 「あたしの練習部屋だけど」
lines.english: “My practice room.”

lines.japanese:
「それはごく一部の使い道だろ！
なんで一般家庭にこんなものがあるんだ！？」
lines.english: “That’s only one tiny fraction of what this room can do! Why does any private home have something like this?”

lines.japanese:
ガラス越しの隣室は、学校の放送室にあるものより、
もう少し豪華な機材で埋め尽くされていて、
それらがここの用途を如実に物語っていた。
lines.english: The adjoining room beyond the glass was packed with equipment more sophisticated than anything in the school broadcasting studio. Its purpose was unmistakable.

lines.japanese:
というか、武也たちがたまに使ってた、
近場のレンタルスタジオよりも遥かに上だ…
lines.english: In fact, it put the local rehearsal studio Takeya sometimes used to shame.

lines.japanese:
「元々は、とある世界的に有名なアーティストの
自宅兼スタジオだったのを、
ウチの母親が設備ごと買い取って」
lines.english: “It used to belong to some world-famous artist—house and studio both. My mother bought the whole place, equipment and all.”

lines.japanese: 「…アーティストって？」
lines.english: “…What artist?”

lines.japanese: 「だから『とある』」
lines.english: “That’s what ‘some’ means.”

lines.japanese: 「本当は正体知ってるよなそうなんだよな？」
lines.english: “You know who it was, though, don’t you? Of course you do!”

lines.japanese: 『世界的に有名』と言ってる時点で…
lines.english: She’d already called the person world-famous.

lines.japanese:
というか、冬馬の母親も立派に
『世界的に有名なアーティスト』だけど。
lines.english: Then again, Touma’s own mother was a perfectly legitimate “world-famous artist.”

lines.japanese:
「しばらく、ピアノ以外使ってなかったから、
昨日まで業者呼んでメンテナンスしてもらってた。
ま、なんとかまだ使えるみたい」
lines.english: “I hadn’t used anything but the piano in ages, so I had people in to service it all. They only finished yesterday. It looks like most of it still works.”

lines.japanese: 「学生の分際で…」
lines.english: “You’re a high school student, for God’s sake…”

lines.japanese: 「悔しかったら親に放っておかれてみろ」
lines.english: “If you’re jealous, try having your mother abandon you.”

lines.japanese: 「さり気なくそういうことをネタにするな、重いわ」
lines.english: “Don’t drop something that heavy so casually.”

lines.japanese: 「なら軽々と突っ込むな」
lines.english: “Then don’t make light of it.”

lines.japanese:
「そういうこと言うと謝るぞ？　謝っちゃうぞ？
ものすごく気まずい雰囲気にしちまうぞ？」
lines.english: “Keep that up and I’ll apologize, you know. I mean it. I’ll make this painfully awkward for both of us.”

lines.japanese:
「………練習するぞ練習。
北原の望みどおり、思う存分合わせてやる」
lines.english: “…Fine. Practice. You wanted to play together, so I’ll play with you as much as you like.”

lines.japanese:
「よろしくお願いします！
…冬馬先生」
lines.english: “Yes, ma’am! …Coach Touma.”

lines.japanese: 「ふん」
lines.english: “Hmph.”

lines.japanese:
どこまで踏み込んで、どこで引くかとか、
まだまだかなりの綱渡りだけど。
lines.english: I was still walking a tightrope, feeling out how far to press and when to back off.

lines.japanese:
そもそも、今までと同じように、
実は今でも踏み込むだけ踏み込んでて、
ただ向こうの許容範囲が広がっただけかもしれないけど。
lines.english: Then again, maybe I was pushing just as hard as ever, and she had simply learned to tolerate more of me.

lines.japanese:
それでも、冬馬と俺の会話は、
春の頃から俺がずっと求めてたように、
少しずつ、歯車が噛み合ってきているって、思う。
lines.english: Even so, I thought our conversations were finally beginning to click—little by little, just as I had wanted ever since spring.

lines.japanese: 「ほら外した」
lines.english: “There. You missed it.”

lines.japanese: 「わ、わかってる」
lines.english: “I-I know.”

lines.japanese:
「あ～あ、今度は
ずれてくずれてく」
lines.english: “And now you're drifting… farther and farther behind.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そっちが段々速くなってるんじゃ…」
lines.english: “M-Maybe you’re gradually speeding up…”

lines.japanese: 「なら次からはメトロノーム使おうか？」
lines.english: “Want to use a metronome next time?”

lines.japanese:
ずっと俺の方を見て、
ずっと俺のミスをあげつらい、
それでも自分はミス一つせず…
lines.english: She never took her eyes off me, never stopped pointing out my mistakes, and never made a single one herself.

lines.japanese:
「いい？　今まではこっちが合わせてあげてたけど、
今度ばかりはそういう訳にいかないからね？」
lines.english: “Understand? Until now, I’ve been matching you. This time, you have to match me.”

lines.japanese: 「お、おう…」
lines.english: “R-Right…”

lines.japanese:
痛感する…
今の俺は『譜面通り』の冬馬の演奏には、
ついていけないって。
lines.english: It was painfully clear: I still could not keep up when Touma played “exactly as written.”

lines.japanese:
「ボーカルはともかく、
シンセはリズム変えたりしないから、
自分からついてくこと覚えないと」
lines.english: “A singer can adjust her timing, but a synth track can’t. You have to learn to follow it yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん…」
lines.english: “Y-Yes…”

lines.japanese:
今まで、どんだけ俺に合わせてくれてたんだ？
どんだけ理不尽な苦労を強いられてきたんだ？
lines.english: Just how much had she been compensating for me all this time? How much ridiculous extra work had I put her through?

lines.japanese:
「あ～あ、全然駄目。
前から思ってたけど、才能ないね北原」
lines.english: “Nope. Still hopeless. I’ve been thinking this for a while, Kitahara—you really have no talent.”

lines.japanese: そんなふうに、楽しそうにこき下ろされたら、俺は…
lines.english: When she was enjoying herself this much while tearing me apart, how could I…

lines.japanese: 「…もしかして、怒った？」
lines.english: “…Did that make you angry?”

lines.japanese: 俺は…
lines.english: How could I possibly…

lines.japanese: 「もう一度最初からお願いします！」
lines.english: “Please—once more from the top!”

lines.japanese: 「はいはい、何度でも」
lines.english: “All right, all right. As many times as you like.”

lines.japanese: 必死で食い下がるに決まってるじゃないか。
lines.english: Of course I was going to keep at it for all I was worth.

lines.japanese: 「こらこら、今度は速い～」
lines.english: “Hey, hey—you’re too fast this time.”

lines.japanese: だって、心地良いから。
lines.english: Because it felt so good.

lines.japanese: 冬馬が、俺のミスを一生懸命探すのが。
lines.english: Touma searching so intently for every mistake I made.

lines.japanese: 冬馬が、俺の拙い指の動きを笑うのが。
lines.english: Touma laughing at my fumbling fingers.

lines.japanese:
冬馬が、俺を貶すために、
いつもは貧しい語彙を、今だけ総動員するのが。
lines.english: Touma mustering every last word in her usually sparse vocabulary for the sole purpose of insulting me.

lines.japanese:
…冬馬が、俺だけを見てるのが。
ずっと俺に、笑顔を向けてるのが。
lines.english: Touma looking at no one but me. Smiling at me the whole time.

lines.japanese: 「はい残念でした」
lines.english: “Too bad.”

lines.japanese:
「もう一度最初から！
くっそ～、いっつも同じとこで引っかかる」
lines.english: “Again from the top! Damn it, I always stumble at the same place.”

lines.japanese:
「一度ハマっちゃうと、
なかなか抜け出せなくなるよね。
ま、今日のところは…」
lines.english: “Once you get stuck there, it can be hard to break out. Maybe for tonight—”

lines.japanese:
「絶対に一度は通す！
今までだって努力で何とかしてきたんだ」
lines.english: “I’m making it through clean at least once! Hard work has carried me through everything else.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、でもさ、そろそろ終電…」
lines.english: “But the last train will be leaving soon…”

lines.japanese:
「え？　なに？
ごめん、聞いてなかった」
lines.english: “What? Sorry, I wasn’t listening.”

lines.japanese: 「………別に、大した話じゃない」
lines.english: “…Never mind. It wasn’t important.”

lines.japanese: 「？　そうか？」
lines.english: “You sure?”

lines.japanese:
「じゃ…リクエスト通り、
もう一度最初から」
lines.english: “Then… from the top, just like you asked.”

lines.japanese: 「ん…んぅ？」
lines.english: “Mm… Hm?”

lines.japanese:
目が覚めると、
そこは明かりが煌々と灯る白い部屋。
lines.english: When I opened my eyes, I was in a white room blazing with light.

lines.japanese:
さっきまで弾いていたはずのギターは、
今や俺の腕の中で抱き枕と化している。
lines.english: The guitar I could have sworn I had been playing a moment ago was now cradled in my arms like a body pillow.

lines.japanese: 「やべ…寝ちまった」
lines.english: “Damn… I fell asleep.”

lines.japanese:
体に掛かっていた毛布を取り払うと、
そもそも『目が覚めた』という表現自体が、
マズいことであると気づくくらいには頭が回ってきた。
lines.english: I pushed off the blanket and slowly came to. Then I realized that the mere fact I'd woken up meant something had gone badly wrong.

lines.japanese:
「ふあぁぁぁ～。
そろそろ帰らないと…冬馬？」
lines.english: “Yaaawn… I’d better get home. Touma?”

lines.japanese:
床で寝たせいでガチガチに固まった背中をほぐし、
ギターをケースに入れつつ、やっと辺りを見回す。
lines.english: Sleeping on the floor had left my back stiff as a board. I stretched it out, put the guitar in its case, and finally looked around.

lines.japanese:
ピアノの前にはすでに人はいない。
そもそも部屋の中に、俺以外誰もいない。
lines.english: No one sat at the piano. In fact, there was no one else in the room.

lines.japanese: 「まいったなぁ…」
lines.english: “Oh, hell…”

lines.japanese:
中途半端に寝たせいでだるい体を無理やり起こし、
地下室の扉を開く。
lines.english: Still leaden from my half-finished sleep, I forced myself up and opened the basement door.

lines.japanese:
もしかしたら、終電が行ってしまった後かもしれず。
だとしたら、深夜のタクシー代は、学生にとっては
痛恨以外の何物でもなく。
lines.english: The last train might already be gone, and for a student, a late-night cab fare was nothing short of catastrophic.

lines.japanese: 「…しかも時計壊れてるし」
lines.english: “…And my watch is broken.”

lines.japanese:
まるっきり見当違いの方向に向いた針に悪態をつきつつ、
俺は数時間ぶりに地上の空気を吸い…
lines.english: Cursing the hands for pointing to a time that made no sense, I breathed the air aboveground for the first time in hours—and…
“Oh.”

lines.japanese:
そして、
どう考えても見てはいけないものに遭遇してしまった。
lines.english: I encountered something I had absolutely no business seeing.

lines.japanese:
「…っっっ！
北原ぁっ！」
lines.english: “—! Kitahara!”

lines.japanese:
「いや待て冬馬！
俺は今、色々と問題を抱えてることに気づいたんだが、
一つ一つ質問していいか？」
lines.english: “Wait, Touma! I’ve just realized I have several problems here. Can I ask about them one at a time?”

lines.japanese: 「人にモノを尋ねる前に向こうを向け！」
lines.english: “Turn around before you ask me anything!”

lines.japanese:
「あ、ああ…
それと俺、起きたばかりで混乱してたんだ。
その辺の事情を汲み取って欲しい」
lines.english: “R-Right. In my defense, I just woke up and had no idea what was going on. Please take that into account.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなこと知るか！」
lines.english: “Like I care!”

lines.japanese: 「…ふぅ」
lines.english: “…Phew.”

lines.japanese:
恐る恐る振り返ると、眼福…ではなく
衝撃的な光景は扉の向こうに隠れてくれたらしい。
lines.english: When I cautiously turned back, the feast for the eyes—no, the shocking sight—had apparently disappeared behind the door.

lines.japanese:
「全くなんなんだ…
自分の家で風呂に入っただけで何でこんな目に…」
lines.english: “What the hell is this? Why am I the one suffering just for taking a bath in my own home?”

lines.japanese: あ、衣擦れの音が…
lines.english: Oh—the rustle of clothes…

lines.japanese: 「え、ええと…まず最初の質問だけど…今何時だ？」
lines.english: “Um… first question. What time is it?”

lines.japanese:
などと、色々と湧き出しそうになる煩悩は、
この際置いておく。
lines.english: For now, I forced down all the impure thoughts beginning to bubble up.

lines.japanese: 「自分の腕時計でも見てろ」
lines.english: “Look at your own watch.”

lines.japanese:
「いやそれがさ、狂ってんだよ。
なんか７時５０分とか指してるし」
lines.english: “No, that’s the problem—it’s wrong. It says seven fifty.”

lines.japanese: 「狂ってるのは時計じゃなくてお前だというオチだな」
lines.english: “The punch line is, the watch isn’t broken. You are.”

lines.japanese: 「…マジで？」
lines.english: “…Seriously?”

lines.japanese:
これで二つ目の疑問…
『どうして外が明るいんだ？』も同時に解けてしまった。
lines.english: That also answered my second question: Why was it light outside?

lines.japanese:
「あたしはそろそろ学校へ行く。
今出てちょうどギリギリだし」
lines.english: “I’m leaving for school. If I go now, I’ll just make it.”

lines.japanese:
「え？　嘘！　俺着替えてないよ！？
風呂も入ってないし、顔すら洗ってない！」
lines.english: “What? No! I haven’t changed! I haven’t showered or even washed my face!”

lines.japanese: 「知るかそんなこと」
lines.english: “How is that my problem?”

lines.japanese:
「そんなことって…どうすんだよ？
無断外泊とか深夜徘徊とかクラブ通いとか、
根も葉もない噂で推薦取り消されたら…」
lines.english: “What am I supposed to do? What if some completely baseless rumors go around that I stayed out all night, roamed the streets after dark, or went clubbing, and they revoke my recommendation?”

lines.japanese:
「男がそんなみみっちい心配するな。
だいたい、無断外泊は事実のくせに」
lines.english: “You’re a man. Stop worrying about every little thing. Besides, you did spend the night out without permission.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、それは…そうなんだけど…な」
lines.english: “W-Well… yes. I did.”

lines.japanese: そう、事実だ。
lines.english: It was true.

lines.japanese:
無断外泊したことも。
それが、初めて訪れた
一人暮らしの女のコの家だということも。
lines.english: I had spent the night away from home without permission. At the home of a girl who lived alone, on my very first visit.

lines.japanese: そう…冬馬かずさの家だということも。
lines.english: At Kazusa Touma’s house.

lines.japanese:
このことを武也が知ったら賞賛してくれるだろうけど、
その後、何もなかったと聞いて口汚く罵るだろうな。
lines.english: Takeya would congratulate me when he heard. Then, once he found out nothing had happened, he'd curse me out in terms too filthy to repeat.

lines.japanese:
「そんなに困るんなら、
一度家に帰って風呂に入って着替えて来ればいい」
lines.english: “If it bothers you that much, go home, take a shower, change, and come to school afterward.”

lines.japanese:
「いや遅刻はマズイだろ。
俺、入学以来一度も…」
lines.english: “But I can’t be late. I haven’t been late once since I started here—”

lines.japanese:
「ああ言えばこう言う…
あたしはもう知らん。勝手にしろ」
lines.english: “Whatever I say, you’ve got an answer. I give up. Do what you want.”
“Ah…”

lines.japanese:
もう一度リビングのドアが開くと、
毎日俺が目にしてる、いつもの冬馬が出来上がっていた。
lines.english: When the living-room door opened again, the Touma I saw every day emerged fully assembled.

lines.japanese:
しかし、いつもと全く同じ外見でも、
その制服に包まれた内部をつぶさにイメージできる
今の状態では…
lines.english: She looked exactly as she always did, but now that I could vividly imagine what lay beneath that uniform…

lines.japanese: 「どうして目をそらす？」
lines.english: “Why are you looking away?”

lines.japanese: 「い、いや、ちょっと…」
lines.english: “No reason. I just…”

lines.japanese: 正視できない…
lines.english: I couldn’t look at her.

lines.japanese:
「じゃ、あたしは先に出る。
これ、鍵渡しておくから、
学校に着いたら返して」
lines.english: “I’m leaving first. Here’s the key. Give it back when you reach school.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、待て、置いてくな。
俺、駅までの道覚えてない」
lines.english: “Wait, don’t leave me. I don’t remember the way to the station.”

lines.japanese:
「なら早く仕度しろ。
そろそろ走らないと間に合わない」
lines.english: “Then get ready. We’ll have to run if we’re going to make it.”

lines.japanese:
「わ、わかった。
すぐ荷物持ってくる」
lines.english: “All right. I’ll grab my things.”

lines.japanese:
またしても冬馬の
『本当はいい奴』に救われた。
lines.english: Once again, I was saved by the decent person Touma pretended not to be.

lines.japanese:
『終電が出る前に起こしてくれればいいのに』と
一言言いたくもあったけど、ま、やめとこう。
lines.english: I wanted to point out that she could have woken me before the last train left, but decided against it.

lines.japanese: 「あ、それから最後に」
lines.english: “One last thing.”

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese:
「その…悪かった。
お前のあられもない姿を見てしまって」
lines.english: “I'm sorry. I saw you… looking like that.”

lines.japanese:
「っ！
忘れた頃に思い出させるな！」
lines.english: “—! Don’t remind me just when I’d forgotten!”

lines.japanese: 「ふあぁぁ…」
lines.english: “Yaaawn…”

lines.japanese: 「なんか眠そうだね？」
lines.english: “You look kind of sleepy.”

lines.japanese: 「昨夜、練習してて気づいたら朝だった…」
lines.english: “I was practicing last night, and the next thing I knew it was morning.”

lines.japanese: 「うわぁ…」
lines.english: “Oh, wow…”

lines.japanese: 昼休み…
lines.english: Lunch break.

lines.japanese:
眠い目をこすりつつ、顔を洗おうと席を立つと、
教室のドアのところで小木曽が笑顔で手を振りつつ、
ごく自然に俺たちを待っていた。
lines.english: Rubbing my tired eyes, I got up to wash my face. There was Ogiso at the classroom door, smiling, waving, and waiting for us as though this had already become the most natural thing in the world.

lines.japanese:
慌てて振り向くと、俺の隣席は見事なまでにもぬけの殻。
こういうときの奴の危機察知能力は本当に恐れ入る。
lines.english: I spun around to find the seat beside mine spectacularly vacant. His nose for danger at moments like these never ceased to amaze me.

lines.japanese:
「風呂も入れなかった…
だからあんま近寄らない方が」
lines.english: “I didn’t even get to shower. You probably shouldn’t stand too close.”

lines.japanese:
別に小木曽と昼飯を食べるのが嫌な訳じゃない。
というか、そこはかとなく嬉しい。
lines.english: It wasn’t that I disliked eating lunch with Ogiso. Quite the opposite: I was secretly rather pleased.

lines.japanese: んだけど…
lines.english: But still…

lines.japanese: 「ほんどだ、髪ぼさぼさ」
lines.english: “You’re right. Your hair’s a mess.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、だからな…」
lines.english: “That’s what I’m trying to tell you…”

lines.japanese:
俺の前髪をさわさわと撫でる小木曽に、
言い様のない威圧感を感じる。
lines.english: As Ogiso ran her fingers lightly through my bangs, I felt an indescribable weight bearing down on me.

lines.japanese:
…正確には、小木曽本人ではなく、
周囲の男子生徒たちからだけど。
lines.english: Not from Ogiso herself, to be precise. From every other boy in the room.

lines.japanese:
「うんうん、頑張ってるんだね北原くん。
じゃ、ごほうびにこのクリームコロッケをあげよう」
lines.english: “Mm-hm. You’ve been working hard, haven’t you? Here—a cream croquette for your reward.”

lines.japanese: 「人の話は最後まで聞こうな…」
lines.english: “Could you at least hear me out…?”

lines.japanese:
俺の皿に小木曽の弁当箱からおかずが移された瞬間、
周囲の空気が皿に…更に重くなった…
lines.english: The instant one of Ogiso's side dishes crossed into my lunch, the pressure from every direction seemed to land on my plate with it. The meal got heavier still.

lines.japanese:
今までの小木曽とは違いすぎるあけすけな態度に、
周囲がついていけてない。
lines.english: Her newfound openness was so different from the old Ogiso that no one around us could keep up.

lines.japanese: …俺も含め
lines.english: Myself included.

lines.japanese:
「そうそう、そういえば噂になってるらしいよ？
軽音楽同好会のこと」
lines.english: “Oh, that reminds me. Apparently people are talking about the Light Music Club.”

lines.japanese:
「噂になってるのは小木曽だけで、
しかも学園祭についてだけじゃないから」
lines.english: “You’re the subject of the rumors, not the club—and they aren’t all about the festival.”

lines.japanese: 「どういう意味？」
lines.english: “What do you mean?”

lines.japanese:
「最近の小木曽、変わったってこと。
色んな意味で」
lines.english: “People say you’ve changed lately. In all sorts of ways.”

lines.japanese:
「だね。
今はすごく楽。やりたいようにやってるし」
lines.english: “Yeah. Everything’s so much easier now. I just do whatever I want.”

lines.japanese: そう、最近の小木曽は無防備だ。
lines.english: Yes. Lately, Ogiso had been completely unguarded.

lines.japanese:
今まで周囲との間に張っていた
誰にでも友好的な『壁』を取っ払い、
特定の相手に対し、あからさまな贔屓をするようになった。
lines.english: She had torn down the friendly “wall” she once kept between herself and everyone else, and begun showing open favoritism toward particular people.

lines.japanese:
「そのせいで、ミス峰城大付的には、
ここにきて予断を許さない展開と言われてるけどな」
lines.english: “Which is why people are saying the race for Miss Houjou High has suddenly become too close to call.”

lines.japanese:
それは、とりもなおさず、
学園好感度ランキング一位の看板を
下ろしてしまったということでもあり。
lines.english: In other words, she had given up her title as the best-liked girl in school.

lines.japanese:
だけど問題なのは、
その自然体な小木曽がまたえらく魅力的なことで。
これがミスコン委員会のオッズを難しいものにしている。
lines.english: The problem was that Ogiso, when she was simply being herself, was even more charming. No wonder the pageant committee was having trouble setting the odds.

lines.japanese: 「三連覇危うし？
lines.english: “Three wins in a row in jeopardy?

lines.japanese:
…それもまたよし、かな。
わたし、普通の女の子に戻りま～す、ってね」
lines.english: Maybe that’s not so bad either. ‘I’m going back to being an ordinary girl!’ and all that.”

lines.japanese: 「…来週のステージって引退コンサートだったのか？」
lines.english: “…Is next week’s performance your farewell concert?”

lines.japanese: 「ふふ…」
lines.english: “Hehe…”

lines.japanese:
皆はあらぬ勘違いをしてる。
『あの小木曽雪菜にとうとう彼氏ができた』と。
lines.english: Everyone had leapt to the wrong conclusion: Setsuna Ogiso had finally found herself a boyfriend.

lines.japanese:
けれどそれは、冤罪もいいところだ。
何しろ小木曽は、俺にも冬馬にも
全く同じような態度を取ってる。
lines.english: It was a grievous miscarriage of justice. Ogiso treated Touma exactly the same way she treated me.

lines.japanese:
つまり、俺に対しての反応は、
純粋な友情に起因するもので、
別に異性を意識したものなんかじゃない。
lines.english: So everything she did with me came from pure friendship. She didn’t see me as a guy at all.

lines.japanese:
「さてと…ごちそうさま。
教室戻って寝てくるか」
lines.english: “All right, I’m done. Think I’ll go sleep in the classroom.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、リンゴ食べるよね？
lines.english: “You’re having some apple first, right?

lines.japanese: はい、ど～ぞ」
lines.english: Here you go.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、だからさぁ…」
lines.english: “No, listen…”

lines.japanese: …冬馬と俺にしかわからないことだけど、な。
lines.english: But Touma and I were the only ones who knew that.

lines.japanese: 「５分休け…ふあぁぁぁ…」
lines.english: “Five-minute brea—yaaawn…”

lines.japanese: 「…なんか眠そうだね？」
lines.english: “…You look kind of sleepy.”

lines.japanese: 「…ちょっとね」
lines.english: “…A little.”

lines.japanese: 「コーヒー買ってこようか？」
lines.english: “Want me to get you a coffee?”

lines.japanese: 「悪い…」
lines.english: “Thanks…”

lines.japanese: 「わかった。ホットのブラックでいいかな？」
lines.english: “Sure. Hot, black?”

lines.japanese:
「カフェオレ。
一番量の多いやつで」
lines.english: “Café au lait. The biggest one they’ve got.”

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「ブラックのイメージだったから」
lines.english: “I had you down as a black-coffee person.”

lines.japanese: 「苦いの全然駄目なんだ…」
lines.english: “I can’t stand anything bitter…”

lines.japanese: 「…はちみつレモンにする？」
lines.english: “…Want honey-lemon instead?”

lines.japanese: 「酸っぱいのも全然…」
lines.english: “I hate sour things too…”

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「…ぷっ」
lines.english: “…Pfft.”

lines.japanese:
「な、なに？
そんなに…変？」
lines.english: “Wh-What? Is that really… so weird?”

lines.japanese:
「（ず…）
はぁぁぁぁ…」
lines.english: “Slurp… Ahhh…”

lines.japanese:
「そういえば北原くんも眠そうだったなぁ。
二人とも頑張るね」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, Kitahara looked sleepy too. You two are really working hard.”

lines.japanese:
「………隠したな。
ま、言える訳ないか」
lines.english: “…He didn’t tell you. Well, I guess he couldn’t.”
“Tell me what?”

lines.japanese:
「弾けるようになるまで寝なくていいって、
言ってあるから」
lines.english: “I told him he wasn’t allowed to sleep until he could play it.”

lines.japanese:
「ほんと、北原くんには厳しいなぁ。
麗しき師弟愛？」
lines.english: “You really are hard on him. Ah, the beautiful bond between teacher and pupil.”

lines.japanese:
「…楽器を下手くそに弾く奴が我慢できないだけ。
みんな綺麗な音を出したがってるのに」
lines.english: “…I just can’t stand hearing an instrument played badly. Every one of them wants to sing beautifully.”

lines.japanese:
「毎日毎日、そんなに厳しくするから、
北原くん、今日はもう帰っちゃったよ？」
lines.english: “You’re so hard on him every single day. No wonder he’s already gone home.”

lines.japanese:
「勝手にすればいい。
弾けるようになれば文句は言わないから」
lines.english: “He can do as he likes. Once he can play, I won’t complain.”

lines.japanese:
「ね、冬馬さん。
こんな調子でわたしたち、
いつになったら全員で演奏できるのかな？」
lines.english: “Touma, how long is it going to take before all three of us can play together?”
“…Tomorrow.”

lines.japanese:
「え、ホント？
なんだ、もうすぐなんだ！
そっかぁ…楽しみだなぁ」
lines.english: “Really? That soon? Oh, good… I can’t wait.”

lines.japanese: 「期待してていいぞ…きっと驚くから」
lines.english: “You can look forward to it. I promise you’ll be surprised.”

lines.japanese: 「…けなしてる割には信頼してるんだね？」
lines.english: “…For someone who talks him down so much, you really trust him.”

lines.japanese:
「ドアが閉まります。
ご注意ください」
lines.english: “The doors are closing. Please stand clear.”

lines.japanese: 「お帰り」
lines.english: “Welcome back.”

lines.japanese:
岩津町駅、２０時１５分。
冬馬は、昨日と全く同じ時間の電車から降りてきた。
lines.english: Iwazucho Station, 8:15 p.m. Touma stepped off the exact same train as the night before.

lines.japanese:
まぁ、行きの電車の中で約束した通りだから、
意外でもなんでもないんだけど。
lines.english: We’d arranged it on the morning train, so there was nothing surprising about her arrival.

lines.japanese:
「今日こそは準備万端だ。
風呂にも入ったし、制服の着替えも持ってきた」
lines.english: “I’m completely prepared today. I showered, and I brought a clean uniform.”

lines.japanese: 「また泊まる気満々だな」
lines.english: “You’re clearly planning to stay the night again.”

lines.japanese:
今日は、授業が終わったらすぐに帰宅して、
着替え、入浴、仮眠、自主練と、昨日できなかったことを、
２時間で全てこなしてここに戻ってきた。
lines.english: As soon as classes ended, I had raced home and crammed everything I had missed yesterday—changing, showering, taking a nap, practicing on my own—into two hours before returning.

lines.japanese:
昨夜のことで痛感したから。
やっぱり『師匠』の教えは偉大だと…
lines.english: Last night had taught me one thing: never underestimate the wisdom of your “master.”

lines.japanese:
「今日は終電までに帰るって。
こいつらは万が一のときのための備え。
これくらい普通だろ？」
lines.english: “I’m catching the last train tonight. These are just in case. Nothing unusual about that, right?”

lines.japanese: 「…あんたが言うと説得力があるのがタチが悪い」
lines.english: “…The worst part is that, coming from you, it sounds convincing.”

lines.japanese:
件の師匠も、あからさまに嫌な顔したけれど、
どうせいつもそんな顔なので全然気にならない。
lines.english: The “master” in question made her displeasure painfully obvious, but that was more or less her usual expression, so I ignored it.

lines.japanese: というか絶対想定してたし。
lines.english: Besides, she had obviously known I would do this.

lines.japanese:
「今日こそは大丈夫！
ノーミスで通したらすぐに帰る」
lines.english: “I’ll get it right today. The moment I make it through clean, I’m going home.”

lines.japanese: 「だといいけどね」
lines.english: “We’ll see.”

lines.japanese:
冬馬は、もうどうにでもなれという表情を浮かべて、
いつものように颯爽と俺を置いて歩き出す。
lines.english: Touma wore the expression of someone who had given up on everything, then strode off without me as briskly as ever.

lines.japanese:
だから俺は、その艶やかな長い黒髪を見失わないよう、
小走りで彼女の後を追う。
lines.english: I jogged after her, keeping that long, glossy black hair in sight.

lines.japanese: 「あ、それと帰り道にコンビニあったっけ？」
lines.english: “Oh, is there a convenience store on the way?”

lines.japanese: 「夕食、食べてこなかったのか？」
lines.english: “You didn’t eat dinner?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、トラベルセット買ってかないと」
lines.english: “No, I need to buy a toiletry kit.”

lines.japanese: 「…本当に帰る気あるのか？」
lines.english: “…Are you honestly planning to go home?”

lines.japanese:
今日も、彼女の指先から零れるはずの、
綺麗な音たちを楽しみにしつつ。
lines.english: All the while, I looked forward to the beautiful notes that would spill from her fingertips tonight.

lines.japanese: 「おあよ～………冬馬」
lines.english: “Mornin’… Touma.”

lines.japanese: 「…たった二日で随分と馴染んでるな」
lines.english: “…Only two days, and you've really made yourself at home.”

lines.japanese: 「二日続けて床で寝たから体の痛いこと」
lines.english: “Two nights on the floor, and every inch of me hurts.”

lines.japanese: 「帰れよ」
lines.english: “Go home.”

lines.japanese:
現在、７時１５分。
念のためにと用意しておいた目覚まし時計が役に立った。
lines.english: It was 7:15 a.m. The alarm clock I had packed as a precaution had proved useful.

lines.japanese:
それでも、睡眠２時間はさすがにきつい。
結局、朝の５時近くまでずっと練習してた。
地下室というのは時間の感覚がなくなるから怖い。
lines.english: Even so, two hours of sleep was brutal. We’d practiced until nearly five. Basements were dangerous places; they robbed you of all sense of time.

lines.japanese:
「今から風呂？
悪い、顔洗ったらすぐ出てくから」
lines.english: “Showering now? Sorry—I’ll wash my face and get out of here.”

lines.japanese: 「今日こそはのぞくなよ」
lines.english: “Don’t peek this time.”

lines.japanese:
「昨日だって覗こうと思って覗いた訳じゃない。
幸福な偶然だったんだよ」
lines.english: “I didn’t peek on purpose yesterday. It was a happy accident.”

lines.japanese:
「そうか、それは気の毒だったな。
…今からのお前がな」
lines.english: “I see. What a pity. …For you, I mean. Starting now.”

lines.japanese:
「冗談だって冗談。
…あ～、気持ちい～」
lines.english: “I’m joking, I’m joking. …Ahh, that feels good.”

lines.japanese: 「だからくつろぐなと」
lines.english: “I said, stop making yourself at home.”

lines.japanese:
顔にかかる冷たい水が、
だらけきった全身を引き締めていく。
lines.english: The cold water splashing my face snapped my whole body out of its stupor.

lines.japanese:
今日は金曜日。
あと一日乗り切れば週末。
朝から晩まで、思う存分練習ができる。
lines.english: Today was Friday. Just one more day to survive, then the weekend—and we could practice from morning until night.

lines.japanese: …体力が保てばだけど。
lines.english: If our bodies held out.

lines.japanese:
「ふぅ、目が覚めた…
あ、そうだ冬馬。
俺、朝飯作ろうか？」
lines.english: “There. I’m awake. Hey, Touma—want me to make breakfast?”

lines.japanese: 「朝なんかいつも食べないけど？」
lines.english: “I never eat in the morning.”

lines.japanese:
「だから授業中寝てばっかりなんだよ。
朝はしっかり摂らないと体起きないぞ？」
lines.english: “That’s why you’re always asleep in class. You need a real breakfast to wake your body up.”

lines.japanese: 「今週は人のこと言えないだろ北原も」
lines.english: “You’re hardly in a position to criticize me this week.”

lines.japanese:
「まぁそれはいいとして、
昨日のお詫びにってことで、どうだ？」
lines.english: “Anyway, let me make it up to you for yesterday. How about it?”

lines.japanese:
「…できるものならやってみれば？
冷蔵庫の中のものは勝手に使っていいから」
lines.english: “…If you can. Help yourself to whatever’s in the fridge.”

lines.japanese:
「馬鹿にするなよ？
トーストと目玉焼きならお手の物だ」
lines.english: “Don’t underestimate me. Toast and fried eggs are my specialty.”

lines.japanese:
それしかできないとも言う。
なんて平均的な男子学生。
lines.english: They were also the only things I knew how to make. The very model of an average high school boy.

lines.japanese:
「ふぅん…そう。
じゃ、頑張って」
lines.english: “Hmm. Okay. Good luck.”

lines.japanese: 「あれは絶対信用してないって顔だな…見てろよ」
lines.english: “That is definitely the face of someone who doesn’t believe me. Just you wait.”

lines.japanese:
俺だって、家に押しかけて、何度もしつこく教えを請うて、
朝まで寝かせず、しかも自分だけ先に寝ておいて、
さらに着替えを覗くだけじゃないってことを見せてやる。
lines.english: I would prove I was capable of more than barging into her house, pestering her for lessons, keeping her awake until dawn only to fall asleep first, and then catching her half-dressed.

lines.japanese: ………どこの最低野郎だ。
lines.english: God, what an absolute bastard.

lines.japanese: 「…うあ」
冷蔵庫、何もないし。
lines.english: The fridge was empty.

lines.japanese:
５分ほどの喧騒の後、
静寂に包まれる第二音楽室。
lines.english: After five minutes of chaos, silence fell over Music Room Two.

lines.japanese:
小木曽は呆然と俺を見つめ、
冬馬は大きく息を吐きながら天井を見上げ。
lines.english: Ogiso stared at me, stunned. Touma let out a long breath and looked up at the ceiling.

lines.japanese:
そして俺は、期待と不安と…
ちょっぴりの自信を持って、冬馬を見つめる。
lines.english: I looked to Touma, hopeful and anxious—and just a little confident.

lines.japanese: 「………できた、よね？」
lines.english: “…We did it, didn’t we?”

lines.japanese:
「………ん。
できたね」
lines.english: “…Yes. We did.”

lines.japanese:
その、待ち望んだ冬馬の『ＯＫ』と共に、
俺の喜びは爆発し…
lines.english: At that long-awaited word of approval from Touma, my joy exploded—

lines.japanese:
「できた！
できたよ北原くん！」
lines.english: “We did it! We did it, Kitahara!”
“Ah…”

lines.japanese: …ようとしたところで、隣の爆風により鎮火された。
lines.english: —only to be extinguished by the blast beside me.

lines.japanese:
「ほら冬馬さん、わたしの言ったとおりじゃない！
北原くんはやればできるんだよ！」
lines.english: “See, Touma? I told you! Kitahara can do it when he really tries!”

lines.japanese: 「は、はは…」
lines.english: “Ha… haha…”

lines.japanese:
これがまた、俺の予想を遥かに越えた勢いで、
こんなに心から喜んでくれることが本当に嬉しくて。
…というか、どれだけ信用がなかったんだ俺。
lines.english: She was happier for me than I'd ever expected, and seeing how much she meant it made me happy too. Though really, how little faith had she had in me?

lines.japanese:
「たった一人でずっと頑張って、
ちゃんと期待した通りの結果を出したんだね、凄いよ」
lines.english: “You worked so hard all by yourself, and you came through exactly the way we hoped you would. That’s amazing.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、それは、実は…」
lines.english: “Well, actually, about that…”

lines.japanese:
「本当だな。
北原を少し侮ってたみたいだ」
lines.english: “She’s right. Looks like I underestimated you a little, Kitahara.”
“Huh…?”

lines.japanese:
どうやって言い訳しようか、
それもどっちに言い訳しようか逡巡した隙に、
冬馬があっさり流してくれてしまった。
lines.english: While I hesitated over how to explain myself—and which of them I owed the explanation to—Touma smoothly swept the matter aside.

lines.japanese: 庇ってくれた、のか？
lines.english: Had she covered for me?

lines.japanese:
「これでやっと１曲目…
まだまだ先は長いけど、
とりあえず今日はここまで」
lines.english: “That’s one song down at last. We still have a long way to go, but we’ll stop here for today.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　もう？」
lines.english: “What? Already?”

lines.japanese:
時計を見ても、まだ５時をちょっと過ぎたところ。
日に日に短くなっていく昼が、
それでも夕方のまま留まっている時間。
lines.english: It was barely past five. The days had been growing shorter, but evening still clung to the sky.

lines.japanese:
今週に入ってから『だけ』は、
こんなに早く軽音楽同好会が解散したことはないのに、
実質的部長は、あっさり練習を打ち切った。
lines.english: Not once since the start of this week had the Light Music Club called it a day this early. Yet our de facto president ended rehearsal without a second thought.

lines.japanese:
「その代わり、明日の朝１０時集合。
シンセの方とも合わせる必要があるし、
次の曲もそろそろ決めないといけないし」
lines.english: “That means we meet at ten tomorrow morning. We need to rehearse with the synth tracks and start choosing our next song.”

lines.japanese:
「集合はいいけど…どこに？
土曜なのにここ使っていいの？」
lines.english: “That’s fine, but where? Can we use this room on Saturday?”

lines.japanese:
「練習場所なら大丈夫。
集合場所は岩津町駅北口で。
北原、部長にも声かけておいて」
lines.english: “I’ve got the rehearsal space covered. Meet at the north exit of Iwazucho Station. Kitahara, tell the president.”
“Ah…”

lines.japanese:
そうか…
とうとう小木曽にも『スタジオ冬馬』お目見えか。
lines.english: So Ogiso was finally going to see Studio Touma.

lines.japanese:
「この土日が第一の勝負どころだから、
今週末は泊まり込みで合宿ね」
lines.english: “This weekend is our first real make-or-break stretch, so we’ll be staying over to rehearse.”

lines.japanese:
「合宿？　うわ本当！？
凄い、泊まれるんだそこ！」
lines.english: “We’re staying overnight? Wow, really? We get to sleep there?”

lines.japanese: 「そんなに嬉しいんだ…」
lines.english: “You’re that excited…?”

lines.japanese:
そして…
とうとう小木曽にも『ホテル冬馬』営業開始か。
lines.english: And Hotel Touma was finally opening its doors to Ogiso.

lines.japanese:
「だって、やっぱりみんなで徹夜しないと、
学園祭って雰囲気にならないんだもん。
そう思わない？」
lines.english: “Of course! It doesn’t feel like a school festival unless everyone pulls an all-nighter together. Don’t you agree?”

lines.japanese: 「ま、まぁ、そりゃそう…かな？」
lines.english: “W-Well, I suppose…”

lines.japanese:
「中学のときなんか、
学園祭前でも泊まり禁止だったから、
先生が見回りに来ると電気消してみんな隠れてさ」
lines.english: “Back in middle school, overnight stays were forbidden even before the festival. Whenever a teacher came around, we’d turn off the lights and hide.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はは…」
lines.english: “Ha… haha…”

lines.japanese:
中学の頃から、そうやって許可も取らず
夜通し学校に残る奴らを見つけては、
強制的に帰宅させる立場にいたけどな、俺は。
lines.english: Since middle school, I had always been on the other side: finding students who tried to stay at school all night without permission and forcing them to go home.

lines.japanese:
「ここに来てからは、
なかなかそういうこともできなくなっちゃったけどね。
lines.english: “Since I came here, I haven’t really had chances to do things like that.

lines.japanese: …主に自分のせいだけど」
lines.english: Mostly because of the way I was acting, I guess.”

lines.japanese: 「小木曽…」
lines.english: “Ogiso…”

lines.japanese:
そういう、泥臭い肉体労働とかには、みんなが逆に
参加させないよう気を使ってたんだろうな。
lines.english: Everyone had probably been trying to be considerate by keeping her away from that kind of messy, hands-on work.

lines.japanese:
…ということは、今年の小木曽は、
今までの二年分の抑圧も含め、
どれだけはっちゃける気なんだろうか。
lines.english: Which made me wonder how far Ogiso intended to cut loose this year, with two years of pent-up energy behind her.

lines.japanese:
「…と、いう訳なんで、北原。
お前には今から大事な使命がある」
lines.english: “Which brings us to you, Kitahara. You have an important mission.”
“Me?”

lines.japanese:
「そう。練習を早めに切り上げたのもそのためだ。
さ、行くぞ」
lines.english: “Yes. It’s why I ended practice early. Come on, we’re leaving.”

lines.japanese: 「どこに？」
lines.english: “Where?”

lines.japanese:
「ですから携帯は常時電源ＯＮにして、
いつでも連絡が取れるようにしておきます。
これは雪菜さんだけでなく、他の２人も同様です」
lines.english: “We’ll keep our phones on at all times so you can always reach us. That applies to all three of us, not just Setsuna.”

lines.japanese: 「それでも誰も出なかったら？」
lines.english: “And if no one answers?”

lines.japanese:
「ここに念書を用意しています。
もし３人の誰もが５コール以内に出なかった場合は、
今後、雪菜さんの門限を午後６時にすると約束します」
lines.english: “I’ve prepared a written pledge. If none of the three of us answers within five rings, we agree that Setsuna’s curfew will be six in the evening from then on.”

lines.japanese: 「６時って…窒息するよ普通」
lines.english: “Six o’clock? You’d suffocate anyone with a curfew like that.”

lines.japanese:
「…娘のことはともかく、
先方の親御さんは何とおっしゃっているのかな？」
lines.english: “…Leaving my daughter aside, what does the other girl’s family have to say?”

lines.japanese:
「…そこなんですが、正直に話します。
冬馬さんの家族は、海外に住んでいるため、
冬馬家には現在保護者はいません」
